title: OpsBridge implementation kickoff - ops & data residency alignment
summary: Kickoff to align on OpsBridge pilot for Redwood Private deployment. Covered network/topology (VPC peering vs private link), data residency requirements, SOC2/SAML questions, and initial success metrics (P95 latency,target cost per 1M tokens). Agreed next steps: share Private deployment runbook, security package, and schedule a hands-on staging access window next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-21 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 43 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM); Rachel Torres (OpsBridge VP Eng), Samir Patel (Infra), Nina Gomez (Security), Tom Walker (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Quick kickoff focused on Private deployment topology, data residency constraints, and security handoff items. Several questions on KMS and audit logs. Action items captured.

00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, and this is Priya our SE and Liam our CSM. Quick roll call?
00:18 Rachel (OpsBridge): Hey Alex, Rachel here. Samir, Nina, Tom are with me. Thanks for doing this.
00:28 Priya (Redwood): Great, super. We'll cover high level plan, network, security, pilot success criteria, and then next steps.
00:40 Tom (OpsBridge): Sounds good, we're trying to be quick - we've got a board sync at 5:00 so if we run long flag it.
00:48 Alex: Totally. First question - what's driving the Private deployment choice vs hosted? Rachel?
00:59 Rachel: Mainly data residency and compliance. We handle PII across EU and US regions and our legal team wants keys and logs under our control, so VPC/on-prem is preferable. Cost and latency are factors but compliance is the gating item.
01:18 Priya: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and we can deliver an audit log stream and dedicated control plane. There are a couple topology options — VPC peering, PrivateLink, or an on-prem appliance — depends on your network posture.
01:36 Samir: Quick interjection: we prefer no peering where possible, PrivateLink is normally our pattern, fewer routing changes. How does your runtime reach telemetry/backplane endpoints then?
01:48 Priya: Good question. For PrivateLink we expose a limited set of egress endpoints. We'll share exact FQDNs and IP ranges. The runtime can be configured to talk only to those endpoints. In peering we'll need some route updates.
02:06 Nina: On KMS — does Redwood support our AWS KMS with CMKs, or do you require use of your envelope keys? Our policy says CMKs must remain in our account.
02:19 Priya: We support customer-managed keys, yes. There's an integration pattern where you keep CMKs in your account and provide access via a cross-account role; we don't hold the raw key material. Small caveat: for some on-prem lockboxes we may need a different handshake but we can cover that in the runbook.
02:39 Rachel: Okay, good. Also audit logs — we need 12 months retention and log delivery to our S3 bucket + Splunk. Is that supported?
02:50 Liam (Redwood): Yes, we can stream audit logs to your S3 and we have a Splunk forwarder pattern. We'll include retention config in the security pack.
03:02 Tom: From product side, primary success metrics are 95th percentile latency under 300ms for our typical prompts (avg token length ~60), and cost under our threshold; we'll share sample payloads.
03:18 Alex: Great — for latency we usually need to know sequence length, concurrency, and batch behavior. If you share example traces we can run a baseline on staging.
03:30 Rachel: We'll send a small set of 50 typical calls and a spike file for 500 concurrent to simulate load.
03:40 Priya: Perfect. Quick note — quantization options and model variants affect latency/cost tradeoffs; we'll recommend model profile choices after initial run.
03:54 Samir: Regarding network egress — what's the minimum set of endpoints for PrivateLink? We need to present this to our network team.
04:06 Priya: We'll provide a one-page matrix: endpoints, protocols, ports, and CIDR suggestions. Expect that in the runbook.
04:16 Nina: On SSO — we want SAML-based SSO with SCIM provisioning. Any blocking items?
04:24 Liam: No blocking, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM groups. We'll need an IdP metadata file and list of admin groups to map.
04:34 Rachel: Great. Security review — do you have a SOC2 package and pen-test reports? Legal asked for around 48 hours.
04:44 Alex: We have an up-to-date SOC2 Type II and an external pen test summary; we can share the security pack after the call. I'll put a link in the follow-up.
04:54 Tom: On timelines — we'd like to run a 2-week pilot in staging, then decide on Dedicated vs Private for production. Is that feasible?
05:03 Priya: Yes. Typical flow: staging access + smoke tests (2-3 days), baseline benchmark (2-4 days), then tuning and pilot validation. Two weeks is doable if we coordinate provisioning.
05:16 Rachel: Who owns provisioning of keys and network?
05:21 Samir: OpsBridge will own VPC and KMS. Redwood will provision runtime and coordinate with our network team.
05:29 Priya: Correct. We'll need a point of contact on your side to accept peering/endpoint requests — Samir?
05:35 Samir: Yep, that's me.
05:38 Alex: Cool. Let's walk through a rough staging checklist — I'll read items and you tell me gaps: 1) VPC endpoints or peering, 2) KMS role and CMK, 3) SSO metadata + SCIM, 4) sample payloads, 5) audit log destination, 6) user list for RBAC.
06:00 Rachel: Those look right. The only add is data residency config per region — we run EU and US tenants separately.
06:08 Priya: Noted — we'll set region pinning in the deployment config and include it in the runbook.
06:14 Tom: A slightly random question — can Redwood run inference in our EU region only, and keep logs in our EU bucket?
06:22 Priya: Yes, region pinning and localized log delivery are supported in Private. We'll cover cross-region egress implications.
06:30 Nina: For compliance, can you show us how audit trails look? Screenshots or sample logs are fine.
06:37 Liam: We'll attach redacted log examples and dashboard screenshots in the security packet.
06:44 Rachel: What's the expected lead time to get staging access once we hand over network details? Two business days?
06:51 Priya: For Private, provisioning can take 48-72 hours after we've validated network and keys. We'll target 48 hours but depends on approvals.
07:02 Tom: Ok. On cost estimation — do you have an example of cost per 1M tokens for the recommended models?
07:10 Alex: We'll pull the Optimize recommendations; initial estimate can be a rough delta between Llama-2-variants and opt-quantized variants. We'll include a conservative estimate in the follow-up.
07:19 Samir: Does Redwood do software-level caching for repeated prefixes? We have a lot of repeated system prompts and don't want to pay each time.
07:27 Priya: Yes, prefix/KV caching is supported; caching policies are configurable. We'll recommend cache TTLs based on your workload.
07:36 Nina: Any concerns about PII in logs? We need to redact or avoid storing raw content in some buckets.
07:44 Liam: We can configure redaction flows and ensure raw content stays in your controlled S3 if required; we'll document options.
07:52 Rachel: Ok this is good. Let's talk about pilot success criteria again: 1) P95 latency < 300ms, 2) error rate < 0.5%, 3) data residency and audit logs verified. If all met, we'll move to contract for Private prod.
08:12 Alex: Sounds reasonable. We'll run a benchmark and return results in the follow-up.
08:18 Tom: Any blockers from Redwood side for staging?
08:22 Priya: We need the network info, KMS role, IdP metadata, and sample payloads. That's basically it.
08:30 Samir: We'll produce that by tomorrow morning.
08:34 Alex: Excellent. A couple of logistics items — I'll send an invite for the 2-hour staging window; Priya will lead the smoke tests; Liam will coordinate the pilot timeline and report cadence.
08:48 Rachel: Great. One last thing - what about model upgrades during pilot? We can't have surprises.
08:55 Priya: We'll pin a model version for the pilot and any upgrades will be communicated with a canary roll-out option. We'll show that in the runbook.
09:07 Tom: Perfect. Quick practical: can you also include the minimal IAM policy snippets we need to create cross-account role for KMS access? That accelerates our infra team's work.
09:17 Priya: Yes — we'll attach policy snippets in the runbook.
09:22 Nina: And pen test summary please.
09:25 Alex: Will do.
09:27 Rachel: OK let's wrap. Thanks everyone.
09:31 Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the runbook, security pack, and a staging slot invite.
09:36 Liam: I'll drop a checklist and pilot timeline in CRM.
09:40 Tom: Thanks.
09:42 Meeting end.

Notes on quality: transcript has occasional mis-attributions and shorthand. Some technical terms may be fuzzy (e.g., "PrivateLink" vs "privatelink"). Links referenced: (will be attached in follow-up) - security-pack.pdf, private-runbook-v1.pdf, staging-invite.
